steps.label: open the Tiles tab
steps.goal: tile authoring lives there, and the key list changes with the tab. Arriving lands on the Tiles page — the authored tiles and a New Tile + row; nothing is open until you ask
steps.recovery: if a text field has the keyboard the number types into it: press Escape first

steps.label: start a tile
steps.goal: a usable tile is a floor and two walls meeting at a corner. N names a new tile — the editor stopped guessing names for you
do: press N for a new tile
steps.recovery: Escape closes the name prompt without starting the tile

steps.label: bring a floor in
steps.goal: a tile with nothing in it has no size and no edges, so the floor comes first — and the floor fills the cell, so it is the one piece the arrows cannot move
do: walk the library with up and down
press Enter on a floor piece
steps.checkpoint: the tile has a piece in it
steps.recovery: if the list is empty a filter is hiding it: press Backspace until the filter clears

steps.label: the floor should be in hand
steps.goal: Enter both drops the piece and hands it to the arrows — the held piece carries a subtle brightness lift that resolves to its true colours on Escape. If the arrows walk the library instead, that is the bug back
do: nothing to press — look at the floor in the 3d view
steps.recovery: press Escape and then Enter again; if the arrows still walk the list, that is the finding

steps.label: bring a wall in
steps.goal: two pieces is where a tile stops being a mesh with extra steps. The arrows will not walk the library while a piece is in hand — that is the door, and this step is a question about it: does Escape feel like the right way back to the list?
do: press Escape to put the floor down
walk to a wall with up and down
steps.recovery: if the arrows move the piece instead of the list, Escape did not land: the panel says which of the two states the tab is in

steps.label: turn the second wall a quarter
steps.goal: two walls side by side are a doubled wall; two walls meeting at right angles are a corner. R turns the focused member a quarter, which is what makes a room possible at all
steps.recovery: if the same wall turns again, it is the focused one — use , and . to step the focus to the other wall, then press R

steps.label: flush both walls against their edges
steps.goal: a wall floating in the middle derives no edge, and this is the corner the kit's own tiles ship with: each wall hard against its edge, the two meeting at the join. Watch whether the flush lands cleanly and the corner closes without a gap or an overlap
do: press Shift and an arrow to flush one wall to its edge
use , or . to focus the other wall
flush it against the other edge, so the two meet at the corner
steps.recovery: if the panel says nothing moved, the piece already fills that axis and it names the axis that would — a wall's thin axis is the one that travels

steps.label: is the tile still one cell
steps.goal: only a one-cell tile is a solver prototype — and a wall flushed to its edge still fits, because centre-to-edge is half a cell and the wall is a tenth of one. If the size line says 1 x 1, this is the smallest usable room-maker the kit can hold
do: read the size line at the top of the panel
if it is bigger than 1 x 1, the line under it names the piece
steps.recovery: focus that piece with , and . and walk it back toward the middle with the plain arrows — not Shift, which flushes it to the edge and grows the tile

steps.label: save it
steps.goal: the kit gains a corner tile and the Map palette can stamp it — this is the moment a sketch becomes usable
steps.recovery: an empty tile is refused by name; so is an id the vocabulary does not accept

steps.label: does the corner tile read as a real tile
steps.goal: the last question no checkpoint can answer. You just built the smallest thing a room is made of — floor, two walls, a corner — and saved it where the Map can use it. Now the feedback: what was smooth, what was friction, and what would you change about tile creation — keys, panels, flow, anything
do: look at the tile in the 3d view
then say what you want changed
steps.recovery: there is nothing to recover here: an answer is the finding
